name: Big Octo
tactic: Stun it from the front with the Boomerang and circle round: the weak spot is behind. Hit its back until it falls and stay out of its way when it charges.
note: The remake redesigned its arena; one source says the spinning spikes are gone (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Lizalfos
chapters: Dodongo's Cavern, in pairs; they return in adult dungeons
weak: Any hit they fail to block
tactic: They take turns: lock on to one with ZL, raise your shield and counter right after its swing. If they hop back, wait; do not let them surround you.

name: Dinolfos
chapters: Gerudo Proving Grounds and Ganondorf's Castle
weak: Like a Lizalfos: right after it attacks
tactic: Tougher than Lizalfos, quick with the sword and they breathe fire. Block, counter and back off when they draw breath.

name: Stalfos
chapters: Forest Temple, Shadow Temple, Spirit Temple and Ganondorf's Castle; a weaker kind lurks in the woods
weak: Right after its swing, or a jump attack
tactic: They block almost everything with their shield. Wait for them to attack, block and answer at once, or use a jump attack. Bombs work too.

name: Poe Sisters
tactic: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy steal the flames of the four torches in the lobby. Track each one down (some come out of a painting: shoot it with the Fairy Bow) and hit her while she shows herself. Meg, the eldest, makes copies: attack the original, who always gives herself away.
drops: Each one returns her flame to its torch; all four open the lift to the boss.
note: In the remake Jo is a deep red.

name: Great Moblin
tactic: It blocks the way with a huge club: each slam sends a shockwave in a straight line. Sidestep the waves and hit it up close, or use bombs (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Flare Dancer
weak: Its core, once its flames are out
tactic: Hit it with the Hookshot to knock its flames off. The core runs away: chase it and slash it before it lights up again. Repeat.

name: Dark Link
tactic: It mirrors your sword and your moves: if you attack head-on, it blocks. Try jump attacks, the Megaton Hammer or Din's Fire; letting go of the lock-on and striking from the side also works.
drops: Opens the way to the Longshot.
note: One review says the duel lost its tension in the remake.

name: Dead Hand
chapters: Bottom of the Well and Shadow Temple
tactic: Let a hand grab you or, in the remake, defeat every hand in the room to force it out. When it surfaces, hit its head several times and back off before it bites; the hands come back.
drops: In the Bottom of the Well, the Lenses of Truth; in the Shadow Temple, the Hover Boots.

name: White Wolfos
tactic: Block its swipes with your shield and counter, or sidestep to hit its back. Its claws freeze you.
drops: Opens the chest with the Iron Boots.

name: Iron Knuckle
weak: It is slow: hit and back off
tactic: Its axe smashes pillars in one blow. In the remake you can block its swings with your shield. Hit it and step back; once its armour comes off it gets faster. One of them is Nabooru, controlled by Twinrova.

name: Deku Baba
chapters: Great Deku Tree, Kokiri Forest, Lost Woods, Forest Temple
tactic: Lock on, wait for it to lunge and cut it down. Cut one that stays upright and it drops a Deku Stick. Big Deku Babas are gone in the remake.

name: Deku Scrub
chapters: Great Deku Tree, Lost Woods, grottos
tactic: Bounce its nut back with your shield. When it gives up it shares a hint (in the Great Deku Tree, a sequence). Mad Scrubs fire three in a row.

name: Skulltula
chapters: Great Deku Tree, Lost Woods, Kakariko Village at night, dungeons
tactic: Wait for it to turn round and hit its belly, or shoot it down with the Fairy Slingshot or the Boomerang. Weak to fire.

name: Gold Skulltula
tactic: Kill it and grab its token (with the Hookshot or the Boomerang if it is far away). Equip the Echo Gem: it blinks and vibrates when one is near. Many only come out at night, and ten appear when you drop Bugs on soft soil.
drops: Gold Skulltula Token (trade them in at the House of Skulltula in Kakariko Village)

name: Skullwalltula
weak: They drop off if the ground or wall shakes
tactic: Do not climb past one: knock it off first with the Fairy Slingshot, the Boomerang or the Hookshot.

name: Keese
chapters: Caves and dungeons; Fire and Ice Keese in the Fire Temple and Ice Cavern
tactic: Shoot them down with the Fairy Slingshot, the Boomerang or arrows, or wait for them to come close. Fire Keese burn the Deku Shield; Ice Keese freeze you.

name: Octorok
chapters: Lost Woods, Zora's River, Lake Hylia and ponds
tactic: It spits mud rocks: bounce them back with your shield or shoot it when it surfaces.

name: Tektite
chapters: Red ones on Death Mountain Trail and in Hyrule Field; blue ones on water
tactic: They hop at you: wait for them to land and strike, or shoot them in the air.

name: Peahat
tactic: When it swoops down at you, hit its roots. It drops larvae that die in one hit; the remake has more of them by day.

name: Stalchild
chapters: Hyrule Field at night; in the remake also as an adult
tactic: They keep rising from the ground all night: do not waste time, move on or sleep until morning. The Bunny Hood keeps them away.

name: Wolfos
chapters: Lost Woods and Sacred Grove, at night and in grottos
tactic: Block its swipes and counter, or circle round and hit its back.

name: Guay
tactic: They circle overhead and attack in flocks: shoot them down with arrows or the Fairy Slingshot.

name: Moblin
tactic: They patrol with spears and charge in a straight line when they see you: step aside and hit them from behind.

name: Dodongo
tactic: It breathes fire forward: circle round and hit its tail. Baby Dodongos explode when they die and swallow bombs: keep clear.

name: Beamos
tactic: Drop a bomb at its base or shoot its eye. In the remake the Mirror Shield reflects its beam.

name: Armos
tactic: They look like statues and wake when touched: back off and hit them from behind, or with a bomb.

name: Bubble
chapters: Several dungeons: red ones near fire, blue, green and white ones in temples and the Bottom of the Well
weak: The skull, once its aura is out
tactic: Stop them with your shield and hit the skull when the aura fades. Blue ones are drawn to bombs. A giant Green Bubble lives at the Bottom of the Well (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Like Like
tactic: It swallows you and steals your shield or tunic: keep your distance, attack from range and shake free at once if it grabs you.

name: Flying Pots and Tiles
chapters: Dungeons: the Shadow Temple, the Fire Temple and others
tactic: They launch themselves at you: raise your shield or break them before they take off.

name: False Door
tactic: A monster posing as a door: it gives itself away when it shifts impatiently. Do not walk up to a door that moves (not yet confirmed for the remake).

name: Gerudo Thief
tactic: If the guards spot you, you get locked up. The ones with two swords fight: block, counter and stay clear of their spins.

name: Leever
tactic: They burrow out of the sand: dash past them (hold A) or kill them as they surface. A large one keeps summoning more.

name: Anubis
tactic: It copies your steps and swords do nothing: burn it with Din's Fire or Fire Arrows.

name: Freezard
tactic: Its breath freezes you: stay out of its way. Hit it several times or melt it with Din's Fire or Fire Arrows.

name: Bari
chapters: Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly, Water Temple; Biri in Jabu-Jabu too
weak: A weapon that does not conduct
tactic: They shock you if you hit them with a sword while they glow: use the Boomerang, the Fairy Slingshot or a Deku Stick. A struck Bari splits into Biri.

name: Shabom
tactic: Bubbles that drift in groups: they pop with one hit or shot.

name: Tailpasaran
tactic: Its head is electric: stun it with the Boomerang and hit its tail.

name: Stinger
chapters: Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly and deep water
tactic: They hide underwater or inside other creatures and leap out when you get close: Boomerang or arrows.

name: Shell Blade
tactic: Wait for it to open up and strike inside, or shoot it. From the front, the shell deflects almost everything.

name: ReDead
chapters: Adult Castle Town (far more in the remake), the royal tomb in the Graveyard, the Bottom of the Well and the Shadow Temple
tactic: Its scream paralyses you; in the remake its eyes glow red first and it rushes you when you are close. The Sun's Song freezes them. Do not walk up from the front: circle round and strike, or use a spin attack.

name: Gibdo
chapters: Bottom of the Well and Shadow Temple
tactic: Like a ReDead: its scream paralyses you and the Sun's Song freezes it. Hit and back off; fire hurts it too.

name: Poe
chapters: Kakariko Graveyard and Hyrule Field, at night
tactic: It fades in and out: lock on and strike when it raises its lantern. Catch its soul in a Bottle.

name: Big Poe
chapters: Hyrule Field, as an adult (10 in all)
tactic: In the remake a bright purple lantern gives each one away. Ride Epona, shoot it with the Fairy Bow and catch its soul in a Bottle to sell to the Poe Collector in Castle Town.
drops: Big Poe soul: 5 earn a Bottle, all 10 a Gold Rupee.

name: Wallmaster
chapters: Forest Temple, Bottom of the Well, Shadow Temple and Ganondorf's Castle
tactic: In the remake it casts a purple glow on you before it drops: keep moving. If it catches you, it throws you out of the area. Hit it while it is on the floor.

name: Floormaster
tactic: Hit it and it splits into three small hands that merge again: finish them quickly, with a spin attack if you can.
